description.from:
As an operator, I want the existing command worker to remain deployable while the new platform is validated, so that parallel migration does not interrupt current workloads.

Feature: Isolated command-worker migration
  Scenario: The portable worker runtime is introduced
    Given the existing Celery command worker remains the active production path
    When the new runtime and AWS service are built and deployed separately
    Then existing Celery entrypoints and infrastructure remain unchanged
    And the new service uses isolated queues, images, configuration, and resource names
    And cutover requires an explicit future decision
description.to:
As an operator, I want the portable command service introduced without modifying unrelated deployed resources, so that validation cannot disrupt existing production workloads.

Feature: Isolated command-service introduction
  Scenario: The portable command service is deployed for validation
    Given the current production resource inventory has been recorded
    When the new companion service is deployed under distinct names
    Then existing Amplify, scoring, and pipeline resources remain unchanged
    And no legacy compatibility behavior is added without evidence of an active consumer
    And activation requires an explicit future decision

title.from: Legacy command execution remains deployable during migration
title.to: Existing production resources remain unchanged during command-service introduction
